title: Quoting timber restoration by scope, hazard and evidence
audience: Timber floor restoration workers and business owners who prepare quotes and variations for timber floor jobs.
learningOutcomes: List the included, excluded and assessed items that a timber restoration quote must show.
Price the time for assessment, containment, extraction, clean-up and handover, not only the sanding area.
Handle a variation found after inspection with written approval before work continues.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: SafeWork SA, Asbestos licences: Class A, Class B and assessor licence (no date shown); ACCC, Consumer rights and guarantees (services) (published and modified 17 July 2026, page metadata).

instruction.heading: Price what the job actually needs
instruction.body: A timber restoration quote that is priced only by the floor area leaves out most of the work. The job includes the pre-start inspection and assessment, the room protection and sealing, the extraction set-up, the grit stages, the screening, the repairs within scope, the finish and its drying time, the damp clean-up, the waste disposal and the walkthrough. Price each stage in the way the business's approved pricing method states. Do not discount the containment and the clean-up, because they are the controls that keep the job safe.

instruction.heading: Price the assessment separately
instruction.body: A pre-start assessment for lead, asbestos or other suspect material is a separate line in the quote. Its outcome decides whether the sanding can be quoted at all. If the assessment finds material that needs licensed removal, that removal is not part of this course and is not quoted as part of a normal timber job. Refer it to the appropriate licensed contractor, and say so in the quote.

instruction.heading: State the exclusions in writing
instruction.body: Structural and subfloor repair, removal of suspect adhesive or vinyl, repair of water-damaged boards, and any stain repair where the cause is unknown are excluded unless they are scoped and authorised separately. Write these exclusions into the quote so that the client understands what the price does not cover. Any item the business is not authorised to perform must be shown as excluded or referred, not priced as if it were included.

instruction.heading: Variations and no promised outcomes
instruction.body: If the floor changes after the first inspection, record the change and get written approval for the variation before the work continues. Under the Australian Consumer Law, a service provider must work with reasonable care and competence, and must finish in a timely manner where no time is agreed. Do not promise an exact final colour or an exact appearance on old timber. Explain that the outcome depends on the species, the finish that was there before, the condition of the boards and the products used, and record that explanation in the quote.

instruction.heading: Licence position stays with the job
instruction.body: A quote does not change the licence position. Before accepting work that may need a licence, notification or accreditation, check the requirement for the state or territory.

procedure: Complete the pre-start inspection and record the defects, the finish and the assessment outcome.
List the included items, each priced by the approved method, including containment, extraction, clean-up and handover.
Show the assessment as a separate line, and state the referral for any licensed removal.
Write the exclusions into the quote, including structural, subfloor and unknown-cause work.
Record any variation found after inspection, and get written approval before the work changes.
Record the licence position for the job and the approval of the quote before it is issued.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks for a price to sand a whole house floor. The inspection shows an unknown finish, a patch of black mastic in the hallway, and a bouncing board near the kitchen.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you present the quote?
workedExamples.reasoning: Quote the inspection and assessment as a separate line first. Do not quote the sanding of the hallway until the mastic is assessed, and do not include removal of the mastic in a normal timber job. Exclude the bouncing board as structural and refer it. Quote the sanding of the sound areas with containment, extraction, clean-up and handover, and state that the finish outcome depends on the existing finish. Get the quote approved in writing, and record any variation before it is performed.

equipmentAndPpe: Quote template with included, excluded and assessed items
Pricing sheet based on the business's approved method

commonErrors.error: Quoting a flat rate that ignores containment, extraction and clean-up.
commonErrors.prevention: Price each stage of the job by the approved method, including the controls.

commonErrors.error: Pricing removal of suspect adhesive as a normal part of a timber job.
commonErrors.prevention: Show the assessment separately and refer any licensed removal.

commonErrors.error: Promising an exact final colour or appearance.
commonErrors.prevention: State that the outcome depends on the timber and the existing finish, and record it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not grant a licence or authority to carry out regulated work. Completion of training is not evidence of a licence.
Asbestos removal is licensed in some jurisdictions. SafeWork SA's licence page (no date shown) describes Class A and Class B removal licences.
Check it before the quote is accepted.

qualityStandard: The quote lists included, excluded and assessed items, and the exclusions are written in.
Each variation is approved in writing before the work changes.
The quote is checked against the business's approved pricing method before it is issued.
documentationEvidence: Signed quote with the scope, the exclusions and the assessment line
Assessment outcome and the licence position recorded for the job
summary: Price the assessment, containment, extraction, clean-up and handover, not only the area.
Write exclusions into the quote, and refer structural and licensed work.
Get written approval for every variation before the work changes.
referencesAtEnd: Official sources to recheck before any job: SafeWork SA, Asbestos licences: Class A, Class B and assessor licence (no date shown); ACCC, Consumer rights and guarantees (services) (published and modified 17 July 2026, page metadata).

knowledgeChecks.question: What belongs in a quote for timber floor restoration?
options: Included items, excluded items, and the assessment step
Only the sanding area of the floor in the room and the hall
Only the client's name, the address and the phone
Nothing, because it can be agreed verbally on site

knowledgeChecks.question: Which item is usually excluded from a timber restoration quote?
options: Stain testing on an offcut
Structural or subfloor repair
The pre-start assessment
Final clean-up of the site

knowledgeChecks.question: A variation is found after the first inspection. What is correct?
options: Do it now and invoice the client later on the whole job at the end
Ignore it and carry on with the job as planned today
Record it and get written approval before the work continues
Use the cheapest product available on the shelf today

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should you not promise an exact final appearance?
options: Clients never ask about it on the job at all, the floor, the room or the look
It is illegal to describe a floor to a client in any words at all or in writing
Colour never matters to a floor at all in use or in the room where it sits
Old timber and existing finishes vary, and the result cannot be guaranteed

knowledgeChecks.question: Who decides whether licensed removal is needed, and who does that work?
options: The assessment and the state rules decide, and a licensed person does the work where required
The cleaner decides alone, and the cleaner does the work on the site, the floor and the room
The client decides alone, and the client does the work on the site and the floor
Nobody decides, so the work proceeds on the day, the site, the floor and the room
